broad.text: His 10 flagship projects lead with AI agents and automation. Each opens in its own window with the numbers and the decisions behind it: Inbound: Scout, the inbox agent Uzair built for himself: read-only Gmail, a live journal, memory and a daily briefing. Backroom: An AI back-office agent for a fictional restaurant group: read documents, reconcile payouts and cite every number. Agent Desk: Two AI agents on one site: Patch looks after a GitHub account, Pitch drafts LinkedIn posts. Order Desk: A customer order from PO to ready to invoice, with document reading, source boxes and line-by-line checks. LoopDesk: A recycling outreach CRM: keep the enquiry, the right person and the next action together. FollowDesk: Review an exact saved follow-up, simulate delivery and keep the outcome linked to LoopDesk. ScopeDesk: Turn an IT asset-disposition enquiry and its inventory into a source-linked, reviewed handoff to LoopDesk. Invoice Ready: Check UAE e-invoice readiness, fix shared customer data and write PINT AE XML that is read back and checked. Quote Desk: Check a quotation's prices and terms, then write its PDF and Word files from one approved template. Content Desk: A publishing system with reviewed versions, asset ownership and a public site readable without JavaScript. Three earlier AI apps are in the Projects folder too: Flowboard, Sayso, Hindsight, each live on the web. Flowboard: A visual workflow builder, a small n8n: connect blocks, press Run, watch each step's real data. Sayso: Say what you need, and the screen builds itself: a service desk for a made-up airline. Hindsight: What your agents did, after the fact: one timeline for every run of four apps. The Data and analytics folder includes twelve independent pharmaceutical studies, not work for MSD: Rx Market Pulse, Payer Access Intelligence, Field Force Planner, Drug Price Watch, Trial Pipeline Benchmark, PharmaEvidence, SignalDesk AI, CampaignOps, Brand Forecast Studio, GCC Market Report, Digital Demand Pulse, Site Health Monitor. And 23 builds beyond the AI apps, from Footnote's FinanceBench measurement and RAG services to a trading research desk, a data warehouse, a chatbot and a game.

broad.q: Which project should I look at first?
broad.text: For AI agents and automation, start with Inbound (Scout), the inbox agent Uzair built for himself, or Backroom, a restaurant back-office agent measured against rules. For front-end and agent interfaces, start with Sayso. For data visualisation and accessibility, Hindsight. For state management and an engine with real tests, Flowboard. For agents that are careful about cost and safety, Agent Desk. For statistics, Quant Copilot. Each one opens in a window here, with its demo, its numbers and the decisions behind it.
